document.source_limit: Manually curated official-source snapshot retrieved 22 October 2026 from the Registrar General's Department pages on obtaining certified copies and on charges; not independently validated, not live output, and not an official application service. Scope: the counter application for a certified copy of a birth certificate through a Divisional Secretariat. The separate online eBMD application, with its own payment instructions, is a different channel and is not covered. An older Government Information Centre page lists Rs. 100 and Rs. 200 for the same two cases; the Registrar General's Department figures of Rs. 120 and Rs. 250 are used. Verify current requirements with the department.

actions.heading: Complete the application
actions.essential: Fill in the form, giving the birth certificate number and registration date if you know them.

source_context.text: Complete the application for the Divisional Secretariat of the place of birth, giving the birth certificate number and registration date if you know them, because this decides which charge applies.

Submit the completed application with the bank slip to the Divisional Secretariat of the place of birth. For delivery by post, enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope. If the birth is registered you receive as many copies as you paid for; if it is not registered you are notified on Form B38.

Submit the completed application with the bank slip to the Divisional Secretariat of the place of birth. For delivery by post, enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope. If the birth is registered you receive as many copies as you paid for; if it is not registered you are notified on Form B38.

actions.explanation_visible: If you are not sure of the number or date, you can still apply; you then follow the search route in the next step.
actions.source_wording:
